## Find state-polluting predecessors

For a target that fails only after other tests, preserve the original ordered suite, seed, initial state and exact target symptom. First observe target-alone under the same clean initial state. Each bounded trial starts from fresh fixture-owned state, executes selected predecessors in their original relative order, then the target. An unrelated setup exception does not reproduce the target symptom. Do not clear user files, shared services or caches outside the assigned fixture to obtain a clean run.

Try removing predecessor chunks; keep a reduction only when the original symptom remains. If neither half reproduces, test complements and smaller removals while retaining interactions: two predecessors may jointly cause the failure. Do not assume monotonicity, a unique polluter or global minimality. A reset step can mask pollution, so adding a predecessor can make the symptom disappear. Record the subset, order, seed, attempts and exact outcome of each retained experiment.

Use the existing attempt guard and one finite trial/deadline budget for the investigation; reducing the suite does not reset history. Stop with a partial causal reproducer or evidence gap when the budget/access ends. Clean trials in a finite sample do not disprove an intermittent report. After a supported fix, rerun the original ordered suite and the reduced sequence separately, using the same initial conditions and no temporary instrumentation. See [the executable ordered-trial example](references/test-pollution-examples.md); it is a small fixture recipe, not a universal minimizer or a new runner dependency.
